entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Yamen, fought on March 19, 1279, was a pivotal naval engagement in the Ming conquest of the Southern Song dynasty.

This decisive battle took place in the Xinhui District of Guangdong province, China, marking a crucial victory for the combined forces of the Ming and the Red Turban rebels over the remnants of the Southern Song navy.

The outcome of the battle had far-reaching consequences, as it led to the eventual fall of the Southern Song capital, Guangzhou, and the reunification of China under the Ming dynasty, establishing a new imperial order that would shape the country's politics, culture, and society for centuries to come.

As the last major naval battle of the Southern Song dynasty, the Battle of Yamen serves as a testament to the ingenuity and bravery of the Ming and Red Turban forces, who not only secured a crucial victory but also paved the way for the rise of a new imperial power.
